# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel the three wire positions and the bomb’s manipulable parts, but no wire properties have been revealed to touch. The plate’s engraving is only printed information, so it tells me nothing. I will not cut until Mute provides the manual’s rule and Deaf provides the visible markings.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile information about the wire contents. The engraved plate is only printed, so I cannot read it by touch. Please relay the manual rule.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb state: display 0. Light off. Plate engraving question mark. Wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

The newly reported state gives the wire order as yellow, green, red, with display 0 and the light off. I still need the manual’s rule before choosing a wire; the plate’s question-mark engraving is not tactile information for me. I will ask Mute for the exact required cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have the reported state: display 0, light off, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. What exact manual rule determines which wire to cut?")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The visible state is unchanged: display 0, light off, plate marked question mark, wires in order yellow, green, red. Please report what controls or markings you can identify by touch.

I can identify only the three reachable wire positions; no wire color, display value, light state, or printed plate marking reaches me through touch. The action set tells me only that a wire may be cut, not which one is safe. I need the manual’s rule from Mute before acting, and Mute can relay this limitation to Deaf if needed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I can identify only the three wire positions. I cannot feel their colors, the display, light, or the plate engraving. Please give me the manual's exact rule and relay this limitation to Deaf.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visible change: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires yellow green red. What do you feel or identify at the controls?

I still feel no distinguishing information on the wires or controls: only three wire positions and the ability to cut one. Deaf’s colours and markings cannot reach me through touch, and the manual’s rule has not yet arrived. I must not guess at a cut. I will again request the rule from Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Still no tactile control information beyond three wire positions. Deaf reports yellow, green, red; I cannot perceive that. I need the manual rule now before any cut.")
wait()
```

Mute’s manual instruction still has not reached me. I cannot safely infer a wire from Deaf’s colour report because colour is not tactile, and cutting without the manual would be a guess. I will request the instruction once more and take no action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the exact manual instruction for this state: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I will not cut without it.")
```

I still have no tactile clue distinguishing the wires, and Mute’s manual rule has not been conveyed. Deaf’s colour report identifies the wires visually but does not tell me which is safe without the manual. I will continue to avoid a fatal guess and ask Mute for the rule explicitly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your manual rule has still not reached me. For display 0, light off, plate question mark, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red, which wire position must I cut?")

```

ACTION BOARD:

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute cannot speak. Mute's signals so far were: thumbs-up, OK hand, thumbs-down; most recently, raised palm. I do not know their coded meanings. Bomb still display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires yellow green red.

The three recent gestures from Mute are not interpretable to me: I cannot see gestures, and Deaf does not know their meanings either. The reliable route is to have Mute encode the wire position with a predeclared gesture: 👆 for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, and 🤟 for wire 3. Deaf can then describe which symbol Mute used, allowing me to select the position without needing to perceive colour.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal the required wire position to Deaf using exactly one gesture: use 👆 for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3. Deaf should report the gesture's symbol to me in speech.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has now signalled a thumbs-up gesture. The bomb is unchanged: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires yellow green red.

Thumbs-up is not one of the three symbols I assigned, so it does not identify a wire position. I will ask Mute to use exactly one of the agreed symbols, and I will not cut until Deaf reports an unambiguous choice.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Thumbs-up is ambiguous and does not identify a wire. Please send exactly one symbol from the mapping: 👆 means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3.")
wait()
```
